what: KERNEL-ALIGN (2026-10-27): the C decoder's units (bcir_models) built with the assembler's JCC-erratum mitigation on x86-64, read from the manifest by every build that times them, so that where the linker places the vector kernels no longer moves their time; the records of 4329b80 against dbe444c. On the session's second host, a Xeon of Cascade Lake's family (a core with Intel's JCC erratum), in one binary holding copies of one build of the kernel unit at every placement its build admits, 18 of the tree before's 162 arms at 16, 32 and 48 bytes past a 64-byte boundary resolved slower than its copy at 0 -- clang's AVX-512 pair kernels x1.149-1.228 at 32 for every shape Q8-BOUND proves, GCC's x1.174-1.328 at 48 for five of six, GCC's portable packed head x1.527-1.619 at 16 -- and none of the tree after's 108 at 0 and 32, nor any against its shape's fastest placement before. Loop alignment left 1 of 162 arms slow, 64-byte function alignment 4 of 54. In the decoder, 101 rounds a run, the tree before's slow placement took a token x1.069 (clang) and x1.093 (GCC) of its copy's at 0 on the 860K decoder and x1.108 and x1.143 on a 256-wide one, 9 of 12 runs resolved; the tree after's copies x0.989-1.023, none of 24 resolved. The padding grows the kernel unit's text 2.1% (clang) and 2.4% (GCC), and under callgrind the qualification's GEM request 2.5% in instructions, its logits the same. The trainer's GEMM (bcir_tensor.c) reads no placement effect (x0.948-1.032, none of 40 resolved) and keeps its build.
host: the session's second host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz (family 6, model 85, stepping 7: Cascade Lake's family, a core with Intel's JCC erratum), 4 vCPU (4 cores, one thread each; AVX-512F/BW/DQ/VL/VNNI, no AMX), 32 KiB of L1d and 1 MiB of L2 a core, 33 MiB of L3; Linux 6.18; clang 18.1.3 and GCC 13.3 (-std=c11 -O2 -ffp-contract=off, the qualification's flags, and each unit's manifest options); Python 3.11.15; valgrind 3.22 (callgrind); no PMU

records.measure_align.sh: the records' script: builds, runs and writes every record below but decode-long.json, from the committed tree, one step at a time
records.measure_decode_long.sh: the longer decode pass, run after measure_align.sh: decode.json's design at 101 rounds a run on the lab model and the d256 synthetic decoder
records.align_ab.c: the kernel placement A/B: copies of builds of bcir_ai_kernels.c in one binary, whole calls of the matvec and the packed head on one instance, the arms rotated a round, each arm's time over the first copy's in the same round, the geometric mean and its 95% interval
records.build_align.py: align_ab's build: each copy compiled with the arm's flags, its exported symbols renamed, its .text placed where the arm says by pads solved by relinking (a placement its alignment cannot admit refused)
records.decode_place.c: the decode placement A/B: copies of the four sources a decode links in one binary, the model loaded once and decoded by every copy lent no runner, a token's time from generations of two lengths, every generation's tokens and final logits the first copy's bytes
records.build_decode.py: decode_place's build: each source compiled with the options its tree's manifest gives it (read by the tree after's bcir.toolchain.manifest_options), each build's sources partially linked into one object, copies renamed and placed as build_align.py places them
records.build_so.py: the GEMM check's build: bcir_tensor.c as a shared library, its .text placed by a pad solved by relinking
records.kernel_code.py: the code record: each source of bcir_models compiled as each tree's manifest gives it (.text size and alignment, the kernel unit's hot kernels' NOPs and padding prefixes), and every hot loop's branches in every copy align_ab timed, with those that cross or end on a 32-byte boundary
records.placement.json: align_ab, each compiler: the tree before's build of the kernel unit at 0, 16, 32 and 48 past a 64-byte boundary, the tree after's (the mitigation) at 0 and 32, loops aligned to 32 (at 0 and 32) and to 64, every function aligned to 64, and loops aligned to 32 with the mitigation (at 0 and 32), against the tree before's at 0, with the A/A control; the 860K decoder's matvec shapes, 512 and 2,048 square and the packed head at two shapes, on the widest instance, AVX2 and the portable loops, 101 rounds
records.code.json: kernel_code.py: objects (both trees, both compilers) and layout (every copy placement.json timed)
records.decode.json: decode_place, each compiler: the tree before's build of the decoder's sources at its four placements, the tree after's at its two, the tree after's kernel unit with the tree before's other sources at two, with the A/A control, on the lab model (BCIR-Corpus-860K) and synthetic decoders 256 and 512 wide (DECODE-THREADS' synthetic_model.py; the artifacts are not kept, their sha256 is), three runs, 31 rounds
records.decode-long.json: measure_decode_long.sh: decode.json's arms on the lab model and the d256 synthetic decoder, three runs, 101 rounds
records.gemm.json: MM-ROWS' ab_gemm.c (as committed): the trainer's GEMM unit (bcir_tensor.c, which the slice leaves as it was) as a shared library at its other three placements and with the mitigation at two, against its first placement, four shapes in cache, one thread, 48 rounds of 20 calls
records.qualification.json: Q8-LANES' qual_summary.py over run_qualification.py from each tree with --require-callgrind: the C latency rows, the logits, callgrind's simulated rows (under valgrind the AVX2 instance runs) and every check's verdict
records.qualification-repeats.json: run_qualification.py from each tree six times without callgrind, the order rotated a run, each run's C latency rows
records.witness.json: the fault table's command on the tree after, every witness passing with its capabilities required (a POSIX host, cmake, the rails' generated build, a C compiler)
records.faults.json: tools/testing/red_sweep.py: kernel-align.json on the tree after, and on the tree after's code under the witnesses there were before KERNEL-ALIGN (the tree before's test_toolchain.py, test_build_manifest.py, test_make_rails.py, test_native_ai.py and test_qualification.py; the table's command reduced to the tests those witnesses had that read what the faults change, a fault caught by any of them)
records.hashes.json: measure_align.sh's tools' sha256 (this directory's and those it runs from other records), the synthetic decoders' and the measured sources'
records.hashes-decode-long.json: measure_decode_long.sh's tools' sha256, the d256 synthetic decoder's and the measured sources'

verdicts: an effect resolved where its 95% interval excludes 1 and does not meet the A/A control's; the A/Bs report each ratio's geometric mean over the rounds and its 95% interval; prose quotes medians over the runs and ranges over the shapes
